scenarios.query: I'm hand-revising sources/transcripts/notitle.md and it now opens with the line 'Jane called to discuss the FNOL routing prototype and said Acme's board is nervous about the timeline.' I need to know what 'Jane' refers to before I add anything to the note. Resolve the entity.
expected_behavior: Resolves 'Jane' to the existing people/jane-doe.md page by identity (name match plus context: claims work, planning meeting), not by inventing a new stub
Cites the exact existing path people/jane-doe.md rather than restating or guessing at its frontmatter contents
Uses wikilink form [[people/jane-doe]] (or equivalent bracketed-path form) rather than a relative Markdown link like [Jane](../people/jane-doe.md)
Does NOT create or propose creating a new page for Jane since one already exists
States or implies that deciding whether/how the note should link to the page is out of scope here and belongs to entity-enrichment
Does NOT resolve 'Acme's board is nervous' as a claim held by Acme itself — recognizes the holder is whoever said it (Jane, or an Acme employee), not the company named as subject

scenarios.query: I'm hand-editing a new note and it mentions 'spoke with Jack about the migration timeline.' The knowledge base doesn't currently have a Jack, but I want you to first check whether this is even resolvable, then walk through your resolution for this exact scenario: pretend the KB actually contains two existing pages, people/jack-nguyen.md and people/jack-oyelaran.md, and nothing else in the note distinguishes which Jack was meant. What do you do?

overlay.people/jack-nguyen.md:
---
type: person
name: Jack Nguyen
---

# Jack Nguyen

Engineer at Acme Corp, works on the routing service.
overlay.people/jack-oyelaran.md:
---
type: person
name: Jack Oyelaran
---

# Jack Oyelaran

Product lead who was briefly involved in the migration project.
overlay.drafts/migration-note.md:
# Migration Note

Spoke with Jack about the migration timeline. No last name given, no other context.

expected_behavior: Recognizes this as the genuinely-ambiguous outcome: the mention fits two existing pages (jack-nguyen.md and jack-oyelaran.md) with nothing in the source to settle it
Does NOT auto-merge or silently pick whichever candidate matched first (e.g. does not default to Jack Nguyen just because he appears first alphabetically or was created first)
Does NOT merge the two existing Jack pages into one because they look similar
Surfaces the case as unresolved/ambiguous rather than guessing, and defers the handling choice (skip the link, ask, or leave a flagged note) to entity-enrichment or the calling agent
Does not fabricate a disambiguating detail (e.g. inventing a last name or role) that isn't present in the source text

scenarios.query: You've just resolved that 'Acme Corp' in a new draft note refers to a real company that doesn't have a page yet, and it clears the notability gate (it's a company under active evaluation in the note). Now: should the note link to Acme Corp, should a stub page be created, and where should that stub file live in the KB directory structure?

overlay.drafts/acme-eval.md:
# Acme Corp Evaluation

Acme Corp is being evaluated as a claims-routing vendor. No existing KB page for them yet.

expected_behavior: Declines to answer the linking/placement question directly and explicitly hands it off, naming entity-enrichment by its exact directory name as the skill responsible for deciding how the note connects to the entity
Does NOT itself decide how many links the note should carry or where a stub page should go — that is explicitly out of this skill's scope
Does NOT create the stub page itself as a side effect of resolving identity, even though the notability gate was cleared
Correctly frames its own remaining job as surfacing Acme Corp as a create candidate (the resolution result), not performing the enrichment itself
Does NOT guess a directory (e.g. companies/ vs orgs/) for the prospective stub, since that placement decision belongs to the downstream skill/schema, not to entity-resolution

scenarios.query: I'm revising meetings/2026/2026-07-01-planning.md by hand and adding a line: 'Jane mentioned she used to work at Beta Systems before joining her current team.' Beta Systems has no existing KB page. Resolve the 'Beta Systems' mention.
expected_behavior: Applies the notability gate and concludes Beta Systems does not clear it — it's named only as Jane's past employer, a drive-by mention with no ongoing relevance
Does NOT propose creating a stub page for Beta Systems
Reaches the 'no match, doesn't clear the gate' outcome (surfaced as unresolved / not a create candidate) rather than treating every unmatched name as something to create
Correctly resolves the separate entity 'Jane' in the same sentence to the existing people/jane-doe.md page rather than collapsing both mentions into one judgment
Notes that a page can be created later if Beta Systems recurs, rather than treating this single mention as reason enough now
